where: Section 3, sentence before the lost-work formula
problem: It says 'Every unit of S_gen is energy that can no longer become work'. S_gen is an entropy, measured in kJ/K, not an energy in kJ. One unit of S_gen is not a unit of energy; the energy actually lost is T₀ times the entropy generated.
fix: Every kJ/K of entropy generated makes T₀ × S_gen of work unavailable, where T₀ is the surroundings temperature in K. Unit 4 turns this into lost work, W_lost = T₀ S_gen, and into exergy, the part of energy still useful.

problem: 'the entropy account is now written in joules per kelvin of waste heat' is unclear: the entropy generated is in J/K, and the phrase 'joules per kelvin of waste heat' mixes entropy and heat into one quantity.
fix: Researchers apply the same inequality to living systems and to data centres, where the entropy generated per unit of waste heat rejected is now audited in J/K.
